description: The Mohamdin Punjabi Warriors are on a mission to transform NASA Earth observation data on soil moisture, rainfall, temperature, and crop health into simple, actionable insights that help farmers adapt to climate change, use water wisely, and protect their harvests. From orbit to the open field, we’re making space data work for those who work the land.
summary:
AgriMatch is a climate-smart agricultural planning platform designed to help farmers make informed decisions about crop rotation and soil sustainability. Developed with Albay, Philippines, as its pilot area, the platform integrates NASA POWER climate data (2015–2025) and SoilGrids soil information to assess crop suitability under local environmental conditions.

Through an interactive interface, farmers can select their location, enter their current three-period crop rotation, and compare it against two alternative cropping strategies. AgriMatch evaluates each option based on climate and soil suitability, crop diversity, and potential soil-building contributions, presenting understandable comparisons to support better farm planning.

By transforming complex environmental datasets into accessible agricultural insights, AgriMatch demonstrates how NASA Earth science data can support climate-resilient farming, encourage sustainable land management, and empower local communities to make more informed agricultural decisions.
details:
AgriMatch is an interactive, map-based decision-support tool that helps farmers in Albay, Philippines, identify suitable crops and explore climate-resilient crop rotations using NASA POWER climate data, SoilGrids soil information, and farm-specific inputs.

Unlike conventional crop recommendation tools, AgriMatch compares a farmer's existing crop rotation with two alternative strategies, highlighting trade-offs in climate and soil suitability, crop diversity, and potential soil-health benefits.

Developed using Next.js, React, Leaflet, and OpenStreetMap services, the platform transforms historical rainfall, temperature, and soil datasets into accessible agricultural insights. Its evaluation considers local environmental conditions, crop suitability, and rotation diversity to support informed planting decisions.

By combining NASA Earth science data with an interactive crop-rotation comparison system, AgriMatch aims to make scientific information more accessible to farmers, encourage sustainable agricultural practices, and strengthen climate resilience in local farming communities.
